Positive sentiment ranges from 1 to 5 and negative sentiment ranges
from −1 to −5. Thus, total sentiment has a range of 2 to 10. Therefore
we subtracted 2 from (positive–negative) to normalize the range from
[2, 10] to [0, 8].
Longevity was measured by counting the number of the days since
the review was created. Length of title and review were measured by
counting the number of words in the text. Helpfulness of a review was
measured as the ratio of “helpful votes” to “total votes” cast by readers
in each review [20,22,46]. Because we cannot directly measure the read-
ership of OCR, we use the total number of votes of a review as a measure
for its readership. People usually vote for a review after they read it.
Hence, total votes can be a good estimate of readership.
4.2. Data collection
A group of 35,000 online reviews of 20 different products were col-
lected from Amazon.com website using the crawler software developed
by the authors. We selected products that had at least 100 reviews. The
examined product types were mobile phones, TVs, laptops, tablets, and
TV mounts. We eliminated the reviews that had less than 4 votes to
ensure that there is a minimum number of votes accumulated for the
review [22]. The ﬁnal sample consisted of 2616 reviews. Fig. 2 shows
the system design of sentiment extraction and mining process.
5. Data analysis and results
We ﬁrst checked the descriptive statistics of the data to determine
the proper data analysis approach. Table 1 shows the descriptive statis-
tics of our sample. Variables in our model including review length and
total votes represent nonnegative and integer data and their standard
deviation is larger than their mean. Hence, the analysis needs to be
adjusted for overdispersion using log-transformation [11].
We also checked the distribution of the sentiment measures to ﬁnd
out how people express emotions in the reviews. Fig. 3 shows the distri-
bution of four measures. As you can see in Fig. 3, review polarity, review
sentiment, and title polarity are normally distributed with the only ex-
ception being title polarity which is skewed to the right. Title sentiment
follows a negative binomial distribution with r = 1 [29]. Negative
binomial distribution measures the number of failures before a certain
number of successes (i.e., r) are achieved.
To analyze hypotheses H1 through H5, we tested the following
regression model:Equation 1Predictors of readership.
We used negative binomial regression to test the ﬁrst model in order
to control for overdispersion assuming that the data follows a negative
binomial distribution [29]. Title sentiment refers to the total sentiment
(positive and negative) available in the title of the review. We created
one dummy variable, TITLE_POSITIVE, to test the moderation effect of
polarity on the effect of title sentiment on readership of reviews. The
variable has a value of 1 for titles with positive polarity and a value of
zero for the others.
Helpfulness is measured as the proportion of helpful votes out of
total votes. Hence, we used binomial regression with logit transforma-
tion to examine hypotheses H6 through H8 using the following regres-
sion equation [6]:Equation 2Predictors of helpfulness.
We created a dummy variable, REVIEW_NEUTRAL, to test the
moderation effect of polarity on the relationship between review
sentiment and helpfulness. The variable has a value of 1 for reviews
with neutral polarity (i.e., polarity = 0) and a value of zero for the
others. We also controlled for the effect of longevity of the review
on its helpfulness by including the log transformation of longevity
in the model.
We checked the correlation matrix for independent variables to
test for multicollinearity. Table 2 shows the correlation matrix for
each equation. Because we observed relatively high correlations
among some variables, we check the VIF of independent variables.
The result of the analysis showed that multicollinearity is not an
issue in this study.
Then we proceeded with model analysis. Both models were signiﬁ-
cant at p b 0.001 level. The ﬁrst model shows a goodness of ﬁt of
1.160 indicating that negative binomial regression was a good choice
for analysis of the proposed model. The proposed relationship between
longevity and total votes was signiﬁcant (b = 0.393, p b 0.001), thus

supporting H1. The relationship between title sentiment and total votes
was signiﬁcant but the coefﬁcient was negative (b = −0.087, p b
0.001). Therefore we don't ﬁnd support for H2. However, the coefﬁcient
for the interaction term Title Sentiment × TITLE_POSITIVE was positive
and signiﬁcant (b = 0.439, p b 0.001). Thus we ﬁnd support for H3. The
relationship between title length and total votes was signiﬁcant but
negative (b = −0.017, p b 0.01). Thus, H4 is not supported. Review
length was found to be a signiﬁcant predictor of total votes (b =
0.355, p b 0.001), providing support for H5.
In the second model, review length is a signiﬁcant predictor of help-
fulness (b = 0.407, p b 0.001) providing support for H6. The proposed
relationship between review sentiment and helpfulness is signiﬁcant
but negative (b = −0.068, p N 0.001). Thus, H7 is not supported. How-
ever, the coefﬁcient for the interaction term Review Sentiment ×
REVIEW_NEUTRAL is signiﬁcant and positive (b = 0.162, p b 0.001).
Thus, we ﬁnd support for H8. Surprisingly, our control variable, longev-

Fig. 4 shows the results of the research model analysis. Table 3 summa-
rizes the hypothesis testing.
Because the effect of sentiment on performance did not completely
match our expectations, we ran post-hoc analyses to explore the differ-
ence between positive, negative, and neutral sentiment. We tested the
ﬁrst model for reviews with positive, neutral, and negative title polarity
separately. Then we ran the second model for reviews with positive,
neutral, and negative sentiment. The results are summarized in
Table 4. Positive sentiment is an important predictor of readership
but not helpfulness. Negative sentiment, in contrast, has negative non-
signiﬁcant effect on both measures of performance. The results regard-
ing neutral sentiment are mixed. Neutral sentiment in the text of the
review improves perceptions of helpfulness. However, reviews with
neutral titles attract fewer readerships.
We also tested the second model for different categories of total
votes to control for the effect of readership on helpfulness. We catego-
rized the reviews into three categories based on total number of
votes: 1–9 votes, 9–99 votes, and 100 votes or higher. We ran the
model for the three categories separately and did not ﬁnd signiﬁcant
differences between them. The only exception is that sentiment does
not have a signiﬁcant effect on helpfulness of reviews with medium
number of votes (10–99). Table 5 shows the results of the analysis.
6. Discussion
This study investigates the effect of review sentiment on readership
and helpfulness of online reviews. Using the theoretical lens of the the-
ory of selective attention we suggest that people read OCR selectively.
We also use theory of selective perception to show how people decide
to read some reviews and ignore the rest. We suggest that because
many consumers read OCR to receive reassurance, reviews with positive
sentiment in the title are more likely to be read. Despite the proposed
positive relationship between sentiment and performance of OCR, we
ﬁnd that sentiment negatively inﬂuences both readership and helpful-
ness of OCR. Emotions have been considered to subvert the rational pro-
cesses [71]. Similarly, we ﬁnd evidence that consumers may perceive
emotional content to be less rational and therefore less useful. The ef-
fect, however, is not consistent across various types of emotions. We
ﬁnd signiﬁcant positive relationship between positive sentiment in
the title and readership of OCR. This observation can be justiﬁed using
attribution theory. It is likely that people attribute negative sentiment
to the author but relate positive sentiment to the product itself. Because
negative emotions are attributed to the author, people are less likely to
read reviews with negative titles. However, if the author expresses
positive emotions in the title of the review, the likelihood of the review
getting attention from consumers will increase. This observation also
conﬁrms that many consumers look for reviews that reassure them
about the choice they have already made [5,24,28].
Unlike our expectation, the effect of sentiment on helpfulness was
not signiﬁcant. This observation may be justiﬁed using elaboration like-
lihood model (ELM) [2]. According to ELM, persuasion occurs through

two routes of inﬂuence: the central route and the peripheral route. The
central route triggers critical thinking in the audience about the argu-
ment of the message and requires high cognitive effort. The peripheral
route to persuasion, in contrast, occurs through positive and negative
cues and undergoes less cognitive effort [2,8,53]. The perception chang-
es by central route are more stable and long lasting while alterations
caused by the peripheral route are less persistent. The sentiment of a
message inﬂuences users' perceptions through the peripheral route
and is expected to be less effective than the cues provided by the central
route. However, certain types of sentiment signiﬁcantly inﬂuence users'
perceptions regarding the helpfulness of a review. The effect of senti-
ment on helpfulness was signiﬁcant and positive for neutral reviews.
It can be argued that a helpful review is a neutral one which communi-
cates both positive and negative aspects of the product. Reviews that
lean toward either positive or negative may be perceived by consumers
as biased and consequently less helpful. Although the use of sentiment

Despite the signiﬁcant effect of title sentiment on the readership of
online reviews, length of the title was negatively related to it readership.
Apparently people use review titles as a quick source of information
about the general theme of the review. Reading and processing longer
titles take more time and demotivates people to read them. Unlike
title length, review length had a positive effect on both the readership
and helpfulness of reviews. Review length can be seen as a signal
about the amount of information contained in the review. Longer
reviews are expected to contain more information and thus attract
more readerships. Moreover, longer reviews are more likely to analyze
different aspects of the product which leads to increased perceptions
regarding their helpfulness.
Surprisingly, longevity has a positive effect on the helpfulness of
online reviews. In other words, older reviews are perceived to be
more helpful. One reason can be the way Amazon sorts the reviews.
By default, users will view the most helpful reviews although it can
also be sorted to display the recent ones ﬁrst. Because older reviews
start receiving votes early, they have a better chance of appearing on
the ﬁrst page which will lead to more votes and perhaps better percep-
tions regarding their helpfulness. Newer reviews, however, stay at the
end of the list and are less likely to receive any attention from
consumers. Aral [3] has a similar observation. He observed that positive
manipulation of helpfulness of online reviews creates a positive social
inﬂuence. As a result, longevity not only affects readership, it but also
inﬂuences perception of helpfulness of OCR.
6.1. Implications
This study has implications for both theory and practice. From a
theoretical perspective, this study introduces a new method of
analyzing online consumer behavior. While previous research ﬁnds
that online reviews signiﬁcantly inﬂuence consumer behavior, few
studies have explored the issue using the textual information contained
in OCR. We suggest that sentiment mining can be utilized to analyze
large amount of OCR that is produced on the Internet every day.
Sentiment mining facilitates processing of big data and is highly replica-
ble. This study also contributes to the body of knowledge by studying
both readership and helpfulness of OCR. To best of our knowledge this
is the ﬁrst study that analyzes predictors of readership of online
reviews. This new performance measure can be used by future
studies to further analyze OCR. We also use three important theories
(i.e., theory of selective attention, theory of selective perception, and at-
tribution theory) to explain how consumers make decisions regarding
reading OCR. Furthermore, although previous research has used the
text contained in online reviews to investigate OCR performance, to
best of our knowledge this study is the ﬁrst to also include the title of
OCR in the analysis. We show that consumers use the title of a review
to receive quick information about its contents. Such information create
a quick impression in consumers which may inﬂuence their decision re-
garding reading the review. Finally, this study can be seen as an initial
step toward action research in the area of OCR. The ﬁndings of this
study and future similar studies can be integrated into a single predic-
tive framework to provide a solution for classiﬁcation and sorting of
OCR [59].

We also have implications for practice. Most previous studies just
use numerical rating and length of reviews to investigate their perfor-
mance. Few studies have tried to analyze the textual information
contained in online reviews which is usually done using human sub-
jects. Although the use of human subjects is useful in explaining how
people use OCR, it barely provides a practical solution for online vendors
because the process is neither scalable nor replicable through automat-
ed systems. However, we use sentiment mining to analyze the text of
OCR. The sentiment mining method used in this study is both replicable
and scalable which provides online vendors with a practical solution for
analysis of OCR.
Our study ﬁnds two weaknesses of the current method used for
sorting OCR. First, we ﬁnd that older reviews attract more readerships.
Many products have thousands of review many of which never receive
any attention from consumers because they stay at the end of a long list
of reviews. Out of the 35,000 reviews we collected for this study, 92.5%
had less than ﬁve votes and 69.7% had no votes. New reviews may con-
tain up-to-date information about the product and the recent changes
made by the manufacturer such as the software updates which may
be overlooked by the current sorting method. Second, we observe that
older reviews are more likely to be perceived helpful than the recent
ones. In other words, perceptions of helpfulness are biased toward
older reviews. These two observations indicate that many potentially
useful reviews receive little or no attention from consumers because
they are barely seen by consumers. Hence, improving the sorting algo-
rithms of online reviews seems to be necessary. An intelligent system
capable of detecting potentially useful reviews can help both vendors
and consumers. It helps consumers by providing them with more valu-
able information and by saving their time and energy. It also helps ven-
dors to satisfy their customers' need for information which will allow
customers to decide more quickly and may eventually lead to increased
sales for the vendors. The ﬁndings of this study can be used by online
vendors to develop systems that analyze and classify online reviews
based on their expected performance.
6.2. Limitations and future research
Like any other studies, this study has limitations. Although automat-
ed sentiment mining is quite useful in analyzing big textual information,
it still has limitations. First, the software we used in this study can pro-
cess different types of textual information. However, it lacks processing
capability for alternate styles of writing such as sarcasm. While there are
many areas for improvement in the ﬁeld of natural language processing,
future research can provide better insights regarding the information
contained in online reviews using more advanced technology. Future
research can also look at how explanation of different aspects of the on-
line shopping experience such as service quality, product quality, and
price inﬂuence OCR performance.
Second, the sample used in this study was collected from
Amazon.com website and was mainly limited to reviews of electronic
products. While the reviews we used in this study are limited to prod-
ucts and do not include services, other websites such as Yelp.com
allow their users to write reviews on services such as restaurants. Be-
cause there are signiﬁcant differences between products and services
[39], the ﬁndings of this study may not be generalizable to reviews of
services. Future research may further investigate the issue by analyzing
reviews of services of other platform. Additionally, while previous re-
search shows that product type has an important moderation effect
on the performance of online reviews, our conclusions may remain lim-
ited to certain product types used in this study. Future research can use
a sample consisting of different product types and test the moderation
effect of product type on the performance of reviews.
Third, the votes casted by readers in each review is subject to imbal-
ance votes bias which indicates that many reviews voted as helpful by
consumers do not contain deep information about the product [41].
Hence, the perceived helpfulness measure may not precisely reﬂect
the actual helpfulness of the reviews.
Fourth, we used the same elements for the calculation of senti-
ment in two different ways: polarity and total sentiment. Using the
same elements for the calculation of these variables may make
them subject to functional dependence and possibly leading to bi-
ased estimation of the relationships in the research model. Although
we believe that functional dependence of these variables is not a
concern in this study, we should be cautious about the application
of these variables.
Finally, our sample lacks language and cultural diversity. The re-
views were collected from Amazon US website and all are in English.
Different cultures express emotions differently. For example, it is be-
lieved that people in individualistic cultures express negative emotions
more freely than those living in collectivist cultures [62]. On the other
hand, language as the vehicle of information may play in signiﬁcant
role in communicating the message to the reader. Future research
may utilize reviews written in other languages to include the effect of
language and culture on the performance of online reviews. Future
research may also look at the differences in expression of emotions
between the real life and the virtual space.

7. Conclusions
This research provides insights regarding the predictors of perfor-
mance of online reviews using a sentiment mining approach. We ﬁnd
that sentiment negatively inﬂuences the performance of online reviews
with two exceptions: positive sentiment in the title and neutral
sentiment in the text of the review. We also ﬁnd that longer reviews
are more likely to attract readership and to be perceived as helpful.
This research can be used by online vendors to create scalable automat-
ed systems for sorting and classiﬁcation of OCR.

chapters.title: Introdução ao Artigo e Estrutura de Investigação
chapters.summary: Apresentação do artigo 'Predicting the Performance of Online Consumer Reviews'. Discussão sobre a importância da caracterização dos autores, revista e o processo de revisão. Identificação das questões de investigação e variáveis dependentes.

chapters.title: Modelo de Investigação e Hipóteses
chapters.summary: Análise do modelo de investigação e das hipóteses. Discussão sobre quais hipóteses foram suportadas pelos dados e quais não foram, focando na correlação entre variáveis.

chapters.title: Natureza do Conhecimento e Teorias
chapters.summary: Discussão sobre o tipo de conhecimento científico (compreensão do mundo) e a classificação da teoria segundo Gregor (preditiva vs. explicativa).

chapters.title: O Método Científico e Richard Feynman
chapters.summary: Reflexão sobre a formulação de teorias e o método científico, ilustrada por episódios da vida de Richard Feynman e a importância da experimentação.

chapters.title: Divagações sobre Ciência e Segurança
chapters.summary: Anedotas sobre o Projeto Manhattan e a natureza humana, relacionando a segurança de cofres com a persistência de comportamentos humanos.

chapters.title: Racional Hipotético-Dedutivo
chapters.summary: Explicação detalhada do racional hipotético-dedutivo, distinguindo entre experimentos laboratoriais e estudos de campo.

chapters.title: Estudos de Campo e Dados Secundários
chapters.summary: Identificação do método de investigação como estudo de campo observacional. Discussão sobre o uso de dados secundários e rastros informacionais.

chapters.title: Estrutura de Dados e Tecnologia
chapters.summary: Análise sobre a natureza dos dados (estruturados vs. não estruturados) e a distinção entre dados secundários de investigação e rastros digitais.

chapters.title: Clarificação sobre Dados Secundários
chapters.summary: Debate sobre a definição de dados secundários e a importância de distinguir dados recolhidos para investigação versus dados de atividade comercial.

chapters.title: Teorias Cognitivas e Formulação de Hipóteses
chapters.summary: Análise das teorias de psicologia e ciências cognitivas (atenção seletiva, atribuição) utilizadas para formular hipóteses plausíveis.

chapters.title: Tecnologias Implícitas e Investigação Básica
chapters.summary: Discussão sobre tecnologias de data mining e sentiment analysis implícitas no artigo. Distinção entre investigação básica e aplicada.

chapters.title: Ambiente de Investigação e DSR
chapters.summary: Avaliação do ambiente de investigação (Modo 1) e exclusão da metodologia Design Science Research (DSR) neste estudo específico.

chapters.title: Técnicas de Recolha e Análise de Dados
chapters.summary: Detalhamento das ferramentas utilizadas, como crawlers e o software SentiStrength para análise de sentimento.

chapters.title: Ética e Conclusões do Artigo
chapters.summary: Discussão sobre questões éticas na recolha de dados online e a utilidade prática do conhecimento gerado para gestores de negócios.

chapters.title: Encerramento e Próximos Passos
chapters.summary: Correção de um lapso sobre o artigo analisado e instruções para a próxima aula, focando num artigo que propõe nova tecnologia.

cornell_notes.topic: Análise Metodológica: Predicting the Performance of Online Consumer Reviews
cornell_notes.subject: Metodologia de Investigação Científica
cornell_notes.executive_summary: A aula focou na análise crítica de um artigo científico sobre a performance de reviews online. O professor demonstrou como identificar questões de investigação, modelos, métodos e o racional hipotético-dedutivo. Destacou-se a distinção entre investigação básica e aplicada, o uso de dados secundários (rastros informacionais) e a aplicação de ferramentas de sentiment analysis (SentiStrength).

cue_column.idea: Racional hipotético-dedutivo (B), baseado em observação de correlações em dados de campo.

cue_column.cue: O estudo é explicativo ou preditivo?
cue_column.idea: Essencialmente preditivo, embora utilize teorias explicativas da psicologia para formular hipóteses.
Dados quantitativos extraídos via ferramentas de mineração (crawlers) e processados por software de análise de sentimento.

cornell_notes.detailed_notes:
### Notas da Aula
- **Modelo de Investigação:** Focado em variáveis dependentes (readership, helpfulness) e antecedentes (tamanho, sentimento).
- **Método:** Estudo de campo observacional (não experimental).
- **Tecnologia:** Uso de SentiStrength para análise de conteúdo (TRL 9).
- **Ética:** Discussão sobre a recolha de dados públicos (rastros informacionais) e privacidade.
- **Contribuição:** Insights para gestores de negócios online sobre ordenação e seleção de reviews.
cornell_notes.glossary:
- [[Racional Hipotético-Dedutivo]]: Método que testa hipóteses através da comparação entre previsões teóricas e observações empíricas.
- [[SentiStrength]]: Ferramenta de data mining para análise de sentimentos em textos.
- [[Rastro Informacional]]: Dados gerados por atividades de utilizadores em plataformas digitais sem propósito de investigação inicial.

metadata.summary: A aula focou na análise crítica de um artigo científico sobre a performance de reviews online. O professor demonstrou como identificar questões de investigação, modelos, métodos e o racional hipotético-dedutivo. Destacou-se a distinção entre investigação básica e aplicada, o uso de dados secundários (rastros informacionais) e a aplicação de ferramentas de sentiment analysis (SentiStrength).

quick: O artigo analisa fatores que predizem a 'readership' (probabilidade de leitura) e 'helpfulness' (utilidade percebida) de reviews online.
As questões de investigação (RQ1 e RQ2) e o modelo de investigação são explicitamente apresentados no artigo, facilitando a identificação das variáveis dependentes.
A teoria desenvolvida no artigo é classificada como predominantemente preditiva, segundo a taxonomia de Gregor, apesar de usar teorias explicativas (psicologia) para formular hipóteses.
O estudo segue um racional hipotético-dedutivo do Tipo B, adequado para estudos de campo observacionais que buscam correlações em dados existentes.
A recolha de dados baseia-se em 'rastos informacionais' (digital traces) da Amazon, distinguindo-se de dados secundários de investigação previamente recolhidos para outros estudos.

detailed.title: 1. Contextualização e Perguntas de Investigação (RQ1 e RQ2)
detailed.text: A aula inicia com a análise do artigo 'Predicting the Performance of Online Consumer Reviews: A Sentiment Mining Approach', contextualizando os autores e o processo de publicação. As questões de investigação são identificadas como muito explícitas: RQ1 questiona quais fatores determinam a probabilidade de um consumidor prestar atenção a uma review ('readership'), e RQ2 investiga quais fatores determinam a perceção de utilidade ('helpfulness') de uma review. Estas questões definem claramente as variáveis dependentes do estudo.

detailed.title: 2. Modelo de Investigação e Variáveis
detailed.text: A partir das questões de investigação, o modelo de investigação torna-se imediatamente aparente. O artigo apresenta um 'research model' claro, onde 'readership' e 'helpfulness' são as variáveis dependentes. As variáveis independentes, ou fatores, que se hipotetiza influenciar estas métricas de performance, incluem características das reviews como longevidade, tamanho, e o sentimento expresso no título e no texto da review.

detailed.title: 3. Classificação Epistemológica e Tipologia de Gregor
detailed.text: O conhecimento gerado pelo artigo é classificado como 'ciência' para 'compreensão', em contraste com conhecimento para um propósito específico. Segundo a taxonomia de Gregor, a teoria produzida é predominantemente 'preditiva'. Embora o artigo utilize teorias explicativas da psicologia (como a perceção seletiva, atenção seletiva e teoria da atribuição) para fundamentar e formular hipóteses plausíveis, o objetivo principal da teoria desenvolvida no estudo é prever a performance das reviews, e não primariamente explicar os mecanismos subjacentes.

detailed.title: 4. Racional Hipotético-Dedutivo e Falsificabilidade (Feynman)
detailed.text: A aula introduz o princípio da falsificabilidade de Richard Feynman, que defende que uma hipótese científica deve ser rejeitada se as observações empíricas a contradizem, independentemente da sua elegância ou da reputação do proponente. Este princípio é fundamental para o método hipotético-dedutivo. O estudo em questão adota o racional hipotético-dedutivo do Tipo B, apropriado para estudos de campo observacionais. Neste tipo de racional, os investigadores recolhem um conjunto de observações e procuram correlações entre as variáveis para testar as suas hipóteses, sem a manipulação controlada de variáveis típica de experiências laboratoriais.

detailed.title: 5. Método Observacional e Dados Secundários vs Rastos Digitais
detailed.text: O método de investigação é um estudo de campo observacional. Os dados são constituídos por 'rastos informacionais' (digital traces) de atividades de compra e avaliação na Amazon, especificamente 35 reviews de 20 produtos. É feita uma distinção crucial: estes dados não são 'dados secundários' no sentido de terem sido recolhidos para um estudo de investigação anterior (Tipo 20), mas sim registos digitais de atividades quotidianas (Tipo 21). A natureza dos dados é mista, com alguns elementos estruturados e grande parte em texto não estruturado.

detailed.title: 6. Ferramentas Analíticas e Questões Éticas/Privacidade
detailed.text: Para analisar os 'rastos informacionais', o estudo emprega ferramentas de 'text mining' e 'sentiment analysis' (como o SentiStrength), complementadas por regressões estatísticas para validar as hipóteses. A recolha de dados de plataformas online, como a Amazon, através de 'crawlers' automatizados, levanta implicitamente questões importantes sobre ética na investigação e privacidade dos dados dos utilizadores, embora estas não tenham sido aprofundadas na transcrição fornecida.

high_yield_concepts.detail: Princípio fundamental do método científico que exige que as hipóteses sejam testáveis e passíveis de serem refutadas pela evidência empírica, independentemente da sua origem ou prestígio.

high_yield_concepts.concept: Tipologia de Gregor (Teoria Preditiva vs. Explicativa)
high_yield_concepts.detail: Classificação de teorias científicas onde uma teoria preditiva foca-se em prever resultados ou relações, enquanto uma explicativa busca compreender os mecanismos e 'porquês'. O artigo em análise é predominantemente preditivo.

Método aplicado em estudos de campo observacionais, onde se formulam hipóteses sobre correlações entre variáveis e se testam essas hipóteses através da análise de dados observacionais existentes, sem manipulação experimental.

Dados digitais gerados passivamente como subproduto de atividades humanas online (e.g., reviews, histórico de compras), que podem ser recolhidos e analisados para fins de investigação, distinguindo-se de dados secundários de investigação.

likely_questions.question: Explique a distinção entre uma teoria preditiva e uma teoria explicativa segundo a taxonomia de Gregor, aplicando-a ao artigo 'Predicting the Performance of Online Consumer Reviews'.
likely_questions.answer: Uma teoria preditiva foca-se em prever resultados futuros ou relações entre variáveis, enquanto uma explicativa visa compreender os 'porquês' e os mecanismos subjacentes. No artigo, embora se usem teorias explicativas (psicologia) para formular hipóteses, a teoria *produzida* pelo estudo é predominantemente preditiva, pois o seu objetivo principal é identificar fatores que permitem prever a performance das reviews (readership e helpfulness).

likely_questions.question: Como o princípio da falsificabilidade de Richard Feynman se relaciona com o método hipotético-dedutivo utilizado no estudo das reviews online?
likely_questions.answer: O princípio de Feynman exige que as hipóteses sejam testáveis e passíveis de serem refutadas pela evidência empírica. No método hipotético-dedutivo, as hipóteses são formuladas e, se as observações (neste caso, correlações nos dados da Amazon) não corresponderem às previsões derivadas das hipóteses, estas devem ser rejeitadas. Isso garante o rigor científico do processo.

likely_questions.question: Diferencie 'rastos informacionais' (digital traces) de 'dados secundários de investigação' no contexto da metodologia de recolha de dados, usando o exemplo do artigo.
likely_questions.answer: 'Rastos informacionais' são dados gerados passivamente por atividades digitais quotidianas (e.g., reviews na Amazon, histórico de compras), sem um propósito de investigação inicial. 'Dados secundários de investigação' são dados que já foram recolhidos e, por vezes, analisados por *outros investigadores* para os seus próprios estudos. O artigo utiliza rastos informacionais (reviews da Amazon), que não foram criados com o propósito de investigação, distinguindo-se de dados de um estudo prévio.

key_definitions.def: A probabilidade de um consumidor prestar atenção ou ler uma review online.
A perceção de utilidade ou quão útil uma review online é para outros consumidores.
Um método científico que envolve a formulação de hipóteses a partir de uma teoria, a dedução de previsões a partir dessas hipóteses e a sua verificação através da observação ou experimentação.
Dados digitais gerados como subproduto de atividades humanas online (e.g., interações em plataformas, compras, reviews), que podem ser recolhidos e analisados para fins de investigação.

problem.text: Volume, variedade, velocidade e veracidade das reviews online que dificultam a sua análise pelos consumidores e empresas.

research_gap.text: Falta de compreensão dos determinantes da leitura (readership) e impacto do sentimento do texto na utilidade (helpfulness).

research_question.text: RQ1: Que fatores determinam a probabilidade de um consumidor ler uma review? RQ2: Que fatores determinam a utilidade percebida da review?

hypothesis.text: Relação entre características das reviews (tamanho, longevidade, sentimento do título/texto) e as variáveis de performance (readership e helpfulness).

contribution.text: Modelo preditivo da performance de reviews baseado em text mining e sentiment analysis para big data.

method.text: Estudo de campo observacional baseado em rastos informacionais de compras e avaliações na Amazon (sem intervenção de laboratório).

dataset.text: Dados secundários de 35 reviews de 20 produtos recolhidos na Amazon via crawler automatizado.

experiment.text: Análise de sentimentos usando SentiStrength e regressões estatísticas para validação de hipóteses.

results.text: Longevidade e tamanho afetam readership e helpfulness; sentimento positivo do título afeta readership quando combinado com texto; certas hipóteses diretas foram rejeitadas.

limitations.text: Dados restritos à Amazon; análise de sentimento limitada pela ferramenta; natureza observacional não prova causalidade direta.

conclusion.text: Classificada como investigação básica confirmatória com teoria predominantemente preditiva segundo a taxonomia de Gregor.
